facts.detail: Ofcom published the Spring 2026 update on 13 May 2026.
The report is a snapshot of fixed and mobile availability as of January 2026.
Full fibre was available to 24.9 million UK residential premises, equal to 82% of homes.
Full-fibre take-up reached 12.4 million premises, equal to 47% of premises with access.
Gigabit-capable broadband availability reached 27.1 million homes, or 89%.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the 2026 planned-deployments report on 13 May 2026.
The report uses network operators' stated deployment plans as of January 2026.
The forward-looking horizon runs to the end of 2028.
The report covers full-fibre and gigabit-capable fixed networks and fixed wireless access plans.
The report supplements, but does not replace, the Spring 2026 snapshot of current coverage.

facts.detail: Ofcom published The Communications Market 2026 on 30 June 2026.
The report is provided as an interactive data portal.
The portal combines industry data, Ofcom consumer research and selected third-party headline figures.
Ofcom points to Media Nations, Online Nation and Connected Nations for detailed sector commentary.
A telecoms-data CSV is listed among the downloadable datasets.

facts.detail: Ofcom's social-tariff guidance was last updated on 22 June 2026.
Social tariffs are intended for households receiving Universal Credit, Pension Credit and certain other benefits.
Ofcom states current social-tariff prices range from £10 to £24.
Most listed social tariffs offer broadband speeds above 30 Mbit/s.
Ofcom says the agreed price should not rise mid-contract and eligible customers can leave without an exit fee.

guard_streams.source: Broadband complaints fall to record low

facts.detail: Ofcom published the Q1 2026 complaints update on 23 July 2026.
The latest figures cover January to March 2026.
Broadband complaints reached an all-time low of six per 100,000 customers.
Ofcom compares the Q1 2026 level with a 2011 peak of 40 complaints per 100,000 customers.
Ofcom says complaints data should be considered alongside price, availability and quality.
